name: Cambodia
description: Cambodia, located in the heart of Mainland Southeast Asia, offers a dynamic business environment with a young, workforce and a rapidly modernizing digital infrastructure. As a Tier 3 country in our hub, it provides significant opportunities for market entry, entity formation, and compliant hiring through EOR and local payroll solutions.

heroData.title: EOR & PEO in Cambodia
heroData.subtitle: Hire compliant teams in Cambodia without a local entity
heroData.description: Thhiya's Employer of Record (EOR) services in Cambodia handle the full employment lifecycle. From compliant labor law contracts to NSSF social security filings, we manage the local complexities while you manage the daily operations.
heroData.bestFor: Companies hiring 1-5 employees for rapid market entry

sections.title: Onboarding Process in Cambodia
sections.subtitle: Timeline: 1-2 weeks
sections.description: A streamlined workflow for integrating local talent into your global team.

steps.title: Contract Drafting
steps.description: Drafting dual-language (Khmer/English) contracts complying with the 1997 Labor Law. Contracts must specify if they are Fixed Duration (FDC) or Undetermined Duration (UDC).

steps.title: NSSF Registration
steps.description: Registering the employee with the National Social Security Fund (NSSF) for healthcare, occupational risk, and the new pension scheme (introduced in 2022).

steps.title: Labor Book Application
steps.description: Obtaining or updating the employee's workbook (carnet de travail) with the Ministry of Labor and Vocational Training (MLVT).

steps.title: E-Visa & Work Permit (Expats)
steps.description: For foreign hires, facilitating the EB-type business visa and the mandatory annual work permit filing with the MLVT portal.

steps.title: First Payroll Run
steps.description: Setting up the KHR (Riel) equivalent payments for tax calculation, even if the base salary is negotiated in USD.

sections.title: Employment Budget (Monthly)
sections.subtitle: Estimating the total cost of employment
sections.description: Summary of mandatory contributions and fees for hiring in Cambodia.

rows.label: Seniority Pay (UDC Only)
values: Average of 15 days salary per year, paid bi-annually

rows.label: EOR Management Fee
values: Flat fee per employee for full compliance management

items.title: Fixed Duration Contract (FDC) Limits
items.text: FDCs cannot exceed 2 years. If renewed beyond 2 years, the contract automatically converts to a UDC (Undetermined Duration Contract) with higher termination protections.

items.title: USD vs KHR Payments
items.text: While most professional salaries are paid in USD, the GDT (Tax office) requires all payroll reports to be submitted in KHR using the National Bank of Cambodia's monthly exchange rate.

items.title: Seniority Pay vs Indemnity
items.text: Since 2019, seniority pay is mandatory for UDC employees. It amounts to 15 days of salary/benefits per year, paid in 7.5-day installments every June and December.

faqs.question: Can I hire expats without a local entity?
faqs.answer: Yes, through an EOR. The EOR acts as the sponsor for the work permit and EB-visa, ensuring the 10% foreign worker quota is managed across their entire workforce.

faqs.question: What is the standard work week?
faqs.answer: The standard work week is 48 hours, typically 8 hours per day across 6 days, though many offices follow a 5-day week by policy.

faqs.question: Are there mandatory bonuses?
faqs.answer: There is no statutory 13th-month pay, but many companies provide a 'Pchum Ben' or 'Khmer New Year' bonus of 0.5 to 1 month salary.

items.title: Soft Skills Focus
items.text: Adaptability and willingness to learn are often prioritized alongside technical certifications in the local market.

items.title: Collective Harmony
items.text: Decision-making often involves group consensus to ensure team cohesion and minimize individual risk.

items.title: Festival Respect
items.text: Significant time should be allowed for major festivals like Bon Om Touk (Water Festival) when planning project timelines.

sections.title: Monthly Payroll Lifecycle
sections.subtitle: Submission by the 20th of each month

steps.title: Input Collection
steps.description: Gathering overtime hours, unpaid leave deductions, and performance bonuses by the 25th of the payroll month.

steps.title: ToS Calculation
steps.description: Applying the progressive Tax on Salary brackets (0% to 20%) to the gross taxable income.

steps.title: NSSF Contribution Deduction
steps.description: Withholding the employee portion of Health Insurance (1.3%) and Pension (2.0%) according to the latest wage caps.

steps.title: Bank File Generation
steps.description: Creating bank-ready files for local institutions like ABA Bank or Canadia Bank for bulk USD/KHR transfers.

steps.title: E-Filing (GDT Portal)
steps.description: Uploading the monthly payroll tax return (ToS) to the General Department of Taxation portal by the 20th of the following month.

items.title: Electronic Payslips
items.description: Dual-language payslips issued via email or mobile app showing gross, tax, NSSF, and net pay.

items.title: GDT Tax Remittance
items.description: Processing and filing of the monthly Tax on Salary (ToS) through the official e-filing portal.

items.title: NSSF Compliance Reports
items.description: Monthly generation of social security contribution lists for healthcare, occupational risk, and pension.

items.title: Seniority Pay Accrual
items.description: Tracking the 15-day annual seniority payment reserve for UDC contracts.

items.title: Standard Overtime Rates
items.text: Standard overtime is 150% of the hourly rate. Night work (22:00 - 05:00) or Sunday work requires 200%, and Public Holiday work requires 200%.

items.title: Fringe Benefit Tax (FBT)
items.text: Non-cash benefits (housing, meals, cars) are taxed at a flat rate of 20% on the fair market value of the benefit, paid by the employer.

items.title: Salary in USD
items.text: While KHR is the official currency, USD is widely used in the private sector. Ensure your payroll system can handle multi-currency accounting for tax reconciliation.

faqs.question: What is the payroll deadline?
faqs.answer: Employers must file and pay salary taxes and NSSF contributions by the 20th of the month following the payment.

faqs.question: Is severance pay taxable?
faqs.answer: Seniority pay for UDC contracts is generally exempt from ToS up to certain thresholds. Indemnity for FDC contracts is taxable.

faqs.question: Are there family allowances?
faqs.answer: Yes, resident taxpayers can claim a small reduction in ToS for children and a non-working spouse (approx. 150,000 KHR per dependent).

items.title: Pchum Ben Bonus
items.text: While not statutory, most employers provide a bonus during the Pchum Ben festival in September/October.

items.title: Expats & Tax Residency
items.text: Expats staying over 182 days are considered tax residents and are subject to ToS on their worldwide income.

items.title: Severance Logic
items.text: For FDC contracts, a 5% severance (severance pay) of the total contract value is due upon completion.

steps.title: Gross Salary Input
steps.description: Starting with the base monthly salary in USD or KHR. Non-taxable allowances are excluded.

steps.title: Dependent Reductions
steps.description: Applying the 150,000 KHR deduction per child or non-working spouse to the taxable base.

steps.title: NSSF Deductions
steps.description: Calculating the employee's contribution to healthcare (1.3%) and pension (2.0%), capped at the official NSSF limits.

steps.title: Tax on Salary (ToS)
steps.description: Applying the progressive tax brackets (0%, 5%, 10%, 15%, 20%) to the remaining net taxable income.

items.title: NBC Exchange Rate
items.text: Calculations use a standard mock rate of 4,000 - 4,100 KHR/USD. Real filings must use the specific rate from the National Bank of Cambodia.

items.title: Fringe Benefits
items.text: Note that non-cash benefits (housing, meals) are taxed at 20% FBT separately and are typically not included in take-home pay calculators.

items.title: Dependent Reductions
items.text: Ensure you select the correct number of children/dependents to receive the 150,000 KHR monthly tax base reduction.

items.title: Net Take-Home Pay
items.description: The final amount the employee receives after all statutory deductions.

items.title: Total Employer Cost
items.description: Includes gross salary plus employer NSSF contributions and seniority pay accruals.

items.title: Tax Liability
items.description: Detailed breakdown of the progressive Tax on Salary (ToS) brackets applied.

items.title: Take-Home Summary
items.description: Quick view of the final amount after all statutory and voluntary deductions.

items.title: Exchange Rate Log
items.description: Documentation of the KHR/USD rate used for each payroll cycle for audit purposes.

items.title: Minimum Wage 2025
items.text: The minimum wage for the garment/footwear sector is $204/month. While other sectors have no statutory minimum, this serves as a baseline for the market.

items.title: Non-Resident Status
items.text: Ensure you correctly identify if the employee is a resident (182+ days) or non-resident, as non-residents face a flat 20% tax.

items.title: Seniority Payments
items.text: Remember that seniority pay (15 days/year) is generally not subject to the monthly progressive Tax on Salary.

faqs.question: Are seniority payments taxable?
faqs.answer: For UDC contracts, seniority pay is generally not included in the monthly ToS calculation but may be subject to different rules upon termination.

faqs.question: Is insurance mandatory?
faqs.answer: NSSF is the only mandatory social security, but calculating for private 'top-up' health insurance is common in the private sector.

faqs.question: How accurate is this calculator?
faqs.answer: This provides a near-exact estimation based on 2024-2025 rates, but final payroll filings should be verified by a licensed local provider.

faqs.question: Are there tax deductions for children?
faqs.answer: Yes, a deduction of 150,000 KHR per child is available if they are under 14 or still studying up to 25.

faqs.question: Is the CBA (Collective Bargaining Agreement) common?
faqs.answer: CBAs are very common in the garment sector, but less so in the white-collar and tech sectors where individual contracts prevail.

items.title: 13th Month Custom
items.text: If providing a 13th-month salary, it must be added to the ToS calculation for the month it is paid.

items.title: Overtime Tax
items.text: Overtime pay is generally added to the taxable salary before applying the ToS brackets.

items.title: Expat Flat Rate
items.text: Remember that non-resident expats are charged a flat ToS rate of 20% regardless of income level.

heroData.title: Incorporation in Cambodia
heroData.subtitle: Set up your legal entity through the 'Single Portal'
heroData.description: Streamlining business registration in Cambodia via the CamDX Single Portal. From Ministry of Commerce (MOC) registration to Patent Tax and VAT filings, we handle the local bureaucracy.
heroData.bestFor: Enterprises committed to long-term operations and local ownership

steps.title: Name Reservation
steps.description: Applying for name approval through the MOC online system. Names must be in Khmer script and an English equivalent.

steps.title: MOC Registration
steps.description: Submission of Articles of Incorporation. A 'Private Limited Company' is the most common vehicle for foreign investors.

steps.title: Tax Registration (GDT)
steps.description: Obtaining the Tax Identification Number (TIN), Patent Tax certificate, and VAT registration within 15 days of incorporation.

steps.title: Bank Account Opening
steps.description: Depositing the initial capital (min. 4M KHR) and providing the bank certificate to the GDT to finalize registration.

steps.title: MLVT Declaration
steps.description: Declaring the opening of the enterprise with the Ministry of Labor and Vocational Training to enable NSSF and work permit filings.

items.title: Qualified Investment Project (QIP)
items.text: Large-scale investments can apply for QIP status via the Council for the Development of Cambodia (CDC) to receive tax holidays or accelerated depreciation.

items.title: Registered Office Requirement
items.text: A physical address in Cambodia is mandatory for MOC and GDT registration. Virtual offices are increasingly scrutinized by tax inspectors during on-site visits.

items.title: The 'Single Portal' Advantage
items.text: Registration is now centralized through the 'Single Portal' (CamDX), which links MOC, GDT, and MLVT, reducing the need for redundant document submissions.

faqs.question: Can a foreigner fully own a company in Cambodia?
faqs.answer: Yes, unlike many neighboring countries, Cambodia allows 100% foreign ownership in most sectors. Land ownership, however, requires 51% Cambodian equity.

faqs.question: What is the 'Patent Tax'?
faqs.answer: It is an annual business operation tax ranging from $100 to $750+ depending on the type of taxpayer (small, medium, or large).

faqs.question: How long does name reservation last?
faqs.answer: A reserved name is valid for 3 months and can be extended for an additional period through the MOC portal.

items.title: Director Residency
items.text: There are no residency requirements for directors. A company can be 100% foreign-owned in most sectors.

items.title: Lease Agreement
items.text: A physical lease agreement for an office is required for VAT registration. The GDT may visit the premises for verification.

items.title: Company Stamp
items.text: The company stamp must be registered with the MOC and is used for almost every official document and contract.

heroData.title: Staffing in Cambodia
heroData.subtitle: Access the vibrant Cambodian talent pool
heroData.description: Connecting your business with skilled professionals, from garment production management to digital tech. We leverage local platforms like BongThom and CamHR to find the best culture fit for your team.

steps.title: Market Benchmarking
steps.description: Advising on salary ranges in USD, including expected allowances (travel, meal, health) common in the Phnom Penh market.

steps.title: Multi-Channel Sourcing
steps.description: Posting on BongThom.com (for general/NGO roles) and CamHR.com (for private sector/corporate roles), plus LinkedIn for expats/senior management.

steps.title: Pre-Screening & Tests
steps.description: Language proficiency checks (English/Khmer/Mandarin) and technical assessment for specialized roles.

steps.title: Interview Coordination
steps.description: Managing interview logistics and cultural bridging during the negotiation phase.

steps.title: Reference & Labor History
steps.description: Verifying past employment and ensuring the candidate has the required 'Labor Book' for compliant transfer.

items.title: Top Sourcing Platforms
items.text: BongThom.com is the largest and most legacy-trusted site in Cambodia. LinkedIn is highly effective for white-collar sectors like Fintech and Real Estate.

items.title: Skills Gap
items.text: There is high competition for mid-level managers with international standards. Often, companies invest in training 'high-potential' juniors to fill these roles.

items.title: Allowances Matter
items.text: Base salary is often just one part of the package. Including health insurance, performance bonuses, and travel stipends is critical for retention in Phnom Penh.

items.title: Social Dialogue
items.text: Open communication about career progression is highly valued by the younger, tech-savvy workforce in Cambodia.

items.title: Local Job Boards
items.description: Deep integration with BongThom, CamHR, and Pelican for broad market reach.

items.title: Expat Recruitment
items.description: Niche sourcing for foreign experts requiring EB visas and work permits.

items.title: University Partnerships
items.description: Direct access to fresh talent from top institutions like RUPP and ITC.

items.title: Telegram Talent Hubs
items.description: Leveraging massive local Telegram channels dedicated to professional job postings.

faqs.question: What is the typical notice period?
faqs.answer: For UDC contracts, the notice period varies from 7 days to 3 months depending on the length of service. For FDC, it is generally based on the contract term.

faqs.question: Are background checks common?
faqs.answer: Reference checks are standard. Formal criminal record checks (Certificate Number 3) are possible but take 2-4 weeks to process.

faqs.question: Is insurance usually provided?
faqs.answer: While NSSF is mandatory, providing additional private health insurance (like Infinity or Forte) is a common perk for professional roles.

items.title: Interview Expectations
items.text: Job seekers often expect structured interviews and quick feedback loops via Telegram or phone calls.

items.title: Work History Veracity
items.text: Hard copies of labor books and certificates are highly valued. Always verify previous employment through direct calls.

items.title: Language Proficiency
items.text: English is widely spoken in the professional community, but testing for written Khmer is recommended for local admin roles.

heroData.title: HRIS in Cambodia
heroData.subtitle: Modern HR management for the Cambodian workforce
heroData.description: Digitize your HR operations with systems tailored for Cambodia's unique labor laws. From automated seniority pay calculations to NSSF-ready reporting, our HRIS solutions keep you compliant and efficient.
heroData.bestFor: Growing teams looking to automate manual HR tasks

steps.title: Seniority Pay Tracker
steps.description: Automatic accrual and 6-month disbursement tracking for UDC employees as per the 2019 Prakas.

steps.title: NSSF Integrated Reports
steps.description: Generating pre-formatted CSV/Excel files for direct upload to the National Social Security Fund portal.

steps.title: Dual-Language Interface
steps.description: Providing Khmer and English accessibility to ensure clarity for all staff levels, from factory floor to management.

steps.title: Leave Management
steps.description: Tracking the 18-day annual leave entitlement plus seniority-based leave increases (1 day for every 3 years).

items.title: Cloud vs On-Premise
items.text: Cloud HRIS is increasingly popular due to better accessibility across multiple locations (e.g., Phnom Penh and Siem Reap offices).

items.title: Data Privacy
items.text: While Cambodia's data protection laws are evolving, ensure your HRIS provider uses secure hosting and role-based access for sensitive employee records.

items.title: Mobile First
items.text: With high smartphone penetration, choose a system with a strong mobile app for employee self-service (payslips, leave requests).

items.title: Time & Attendance
items.description: Integration with biometric scanners (FaceID/Fingerprint) for accurate overtime calculation.

items.title: Document DMS
items.description: Digital storage for labor contracts, passports, and MLVT workbook copies.

items.title: KPI Dashboard
items.description: Visual performance tracking for individual employees and departmental targets.

faqs.question: Does the system handle public holidays?
faqs.answer: Yes, Cambodian systems automatically update with the annual Ministry of Labor holiday calendar (approx 20+ days).

faqs.question: Can I integrate with my payroll?
faqs.answer: Most local HRIS systems provide API or flat-file exports to accounting software like QuickBooks and Xero.

faqs.question: Does it support NSSF e-filing?
faqs.answer: Premium localized systems generate the exact .csv or .xlsx format required for a one-click upload to the NSSF portal.

faqs.question: Can I track seniority pay?
faqs.answer: Yes, localized HRIS modules specifically track the 15-day annual seniority accrual for UDC contracts.

items.title: Mobile First
items.text: HRIS platforms with a robust mobile app see much higher engagement from the Cambodian workforce.

items.title: Internet Stability
items.text: Cloud-based solutions are standard in Phnom Penh, but ensure the system works well on mobile data for remote sites.

items.title: Language Support
items.text: A Khmer-language interface significantly reduces user error for non-managerial staff.

heroData.title: Accounting in Cambodia
heroData.subtitle: Professional bookkeeping and tax compliance
heroData.description: Ensuring your business meets Cambodian Financial Reporting Standards (CFRS) and GDT requirements. From daily bookkeeping to monthly VAT filings and annual audits.
heroData.bestFor: SMEs and multinationals needing local tax hygiene

steps.title: Transaction Recording
steps.description: Daily recording of USD and KHR transactions following the Cambodia Accounting Standards (CAS).

steps.title: VAT Reporting
steps.description: Reconciling input and output VAT (standard rate 10%) for the monthly GDT submission.

steps.title: Prepayment of Tax (PTOI)
steps.description: Calculating the 1% Prepayment of Tax on Income (PTOI) based on monthly turnover.

steps.title: Withholding Tax (WHT)
steps.description: Managing 15% WHT for resident services and 14% for non-resident payments.

items.title: CIFRS vs CIFRS for SMEs
items.text: Cambodia adopted IFRS-based standards. Most businesses use CIFRS for SMEs, while public interest entities must use full CIFRS.

items.title: Audit Thresholds
items.text: Enterprises with turnover > 4 billion KHR (~$1M USD) or assets > 3 billion KHR must have their financial statements audited by a certified firm.

items.title: Electronic Invoicing
items.text: Ensure your accounting system can generate GDT-compliant invoices with serial numbers and proper Khmer/English headers.

items.title: Monthly Bookkeeping
items.description: Maintenance of General Ledger, AR/AP, and bank reconciliations in compliance with CAS/CFRS.

items.title: Year-End Audit Coordination
items.description: Preparation of financial statements and liaison with ACAR-licensed auditors.

items.title: Fixed Asset Management
items.description: Tracking and depreciation of business assets according to Cambodian tax rules.

items.title: Inventory Audits
items.description: Periodic physical count reconciliation with digital records for retail and manufacturing.

faqs.question: What is the standard VAT rate?
faqs.answer: The standard VAT rate is 10% on most goods and services. Exports are zero-rated.

faqs.question: Are there different tax years?
faqs.answer: The standard tax year in Cambodia is the calendar year (Jan 1 to Dec 31). Requesting a different period requires MOC/GDT approval.

faqs.question: Is online filing mandatory?
faqs.answer: Yes, the GDT now requires almost all taxpayers to use the e-Filing and e-Payment systems for monthly and annual returns.

items.title: Language of Records
items.text: Accounting records must be maintained in Khmer. English dual-recording is common for international firms.

items.title: ACAR Registration
items.text: All businesses must register with the Accounting and Auditing Regulator (ACAR) to obtain their reporting ID.

items.title: Fiscal Year
items.text: The standard fiscal year follows the calendar year (Jan 1 to Dec 31). Changes require GDT approval.

steps.title: MOC Annual Declaration
steps.description: The Annual Declaration of Commercial Enterprise (ADCO) must be filed with the Ministry of Commerce annually.

steps.title: ACAR Registration
steps.description: Registering your accounting records and financial statements with the Accounting and Auditing Regulator (ACAR).

steps.title: Labor Law Audit
steps.description: Facilitating the annual labor inspector visit and keeping worker books/registries in compliance with the MLVT standards.

steps.title: CDC Compliance (QIPs)
steps.description: For QIP entities, filing for the Certificate of Compliance (COC) to maintain tax holiday status.

items.title: Digital Transformation
items.text: Nearly all Cambodian ministries (MOC, GDT, MLVT) now use digital portals. Physical submissions are becoming the exception rather than the rule.

items.title: High Penalties
items.text: Late filings with ACAR or MOC carry hefty fines ($500+). Automated reminders and professional oversight are highly recommended.

items.title: Foreign Worker Quota
items.text: Ensure your local-to-foreign worker ratio stays within the 10% cap. If exceeded, a 'special request' justification must be filed with the MLVT.

items.title: MOC Annual Declaration
items.description: Online filing with the Ministry of Commerce to keep company data current.

items.title: NSSF Monthly Reporting
items.description: Submission of employee lists and contribution payments by the 15th of each month.

items.title: GDT Monthly Tax Return
items.description: Compulsory e-filing of all relevant taxes via the GDT portal by the 20th.

items.title: Labor Inspection Prep
items.description: Assisting with the documentation required for annual labor department audits.

faqs.question: What is the penalty for late ADCO?
faqs.answer: Missing the Ministry of Commerce annual declaration can result in administrative fines and potential company suspension.

faqs.question: Are board resolutions required?
faqs.answer: Yes, major changes in directors, capital, or shareholders require board resolutions filed with the MOC within 15 days.

faqs.question: What happens if I miss a GDT deadline?
faqs.answer: Late filings incur penalties starting from 2,000,000 KHR (~$500) plus 1.5% - 2% monthly interest on the unpaid tax.

faqs.question: Is an external audit always mandatory?
faqs.answer: Entities meeting two of three criteria (Revenue > $1M, Assets > $0.75M, Employees > 100) are subject to mandatory external audit.

faqs.question: What is the ACAR filing?
faqs.answer: The Accounting and Auditing Regulator (ACAR) requires all enterprises to submit their financial reports electronically regardless of audit status.

items.title: Transparency Portals
items.text: Cambodia has digitized many registration processes (e.g., CamDX), making compliance easier to track online.

items.title: Public Holidays
items.text: Cambodia has many public holidays (approx. 20-22 days). Ensure your compliance calendar accounts for office closures.

items.title: Ministry Liaison
items.text: Building a good working relationship with local ministry officers can help expedite manual verification processes.

steps.title: Monthly VAT & WHT
steps.description: Filing 10% VAT and various Withholding Tax rates (15% for resident services/rent) by the 20th of each month.

steps.title: Patent Tax Renewal
steps.description: Annual renewal of the business license (Patent Tax) by March 31st each year.

steps.title: Tax on Income (ToI)
steps.description: Annual declaration of corporate profit tax (standard 20%) due by March 31st for the previous calendar year.

steps.title: Double Tax Agreements
steps.description: Leveraging DTAs with countries like Singapore, China, and South Korea to reduce withholding rates on dividends and interest.

items.title: Monthly Tax Returns
items.description: Preparation and e-filing of VAT, Withholding Tax, and Prepayment of Tax on Income.

items.title: Annual Patent Tax
items.description: Processing the mandatory annual business tax based on the company's revenue level.

items.title: Annual Tax on Income
items.description: Filing the year-end corporate income tax return (ToI) by March 31st.

items.title: Stamp Duty Processing
items.description: Payment of 0.1% stamp duty on legal documents and property transfers.

items.title: Strict Enforcement
items.text: The GDT has modernized significantly. Automated e-filing systems make it easier for authorities to flag late filings or inconsistent data across reports.

items.title: Capital Gains Tax
items.text: A new 20% Capital Gains Tax was delayed multiple times and is currently scheduled for implementation in 2024/2025. Monitor closely.

items.title: Incentive Status
items.text: New Investment Law (2021) provides enhanced incentives (longer tax holidays) for prioritized sectors like Agrotech and green energy.

faqs.question: What is the Minimum Tax?
faqs.answer: The Minimum Tax is a 1% tax on annual turnover, payable if it exceeds the annual Tax on Income (unless the entity is a QIP).

faqs.question: Does Cambodia have a GST?
faqs.answer: Cambodia uses VAT (Value Added Tax) instead of GST, currently capped at a standard 10% rate.

faqs.question: What is the VAT rate?
faqs.answer: The standard VAT rate is 10% for domestic supplies and 0% for exported goods and services.

faqs.question: How often must I pay Patent Tax?
faqs.answer: Patent Tax is an annual obligation paid between January 1st and March 31st of each year.

faqs.question: Is there a capital gains tax?
faqs.answer: A 20% Capital Gains Tax was announced but its implementation has been deferred multiple times (latest deferral to 2025/2026).

items.title: QIP Status
items.text: Qualified Investment Projects (QIP) can enjoy profit tax holidays of up to 9 years or special depreciation rates.

items.title: Small Business Support
items.text: Small taxpayers (revenue < $62.5k) have much simpler flat-rate tax requirements compared to larger entities.

items.title: SME Tax Holidays
items.text: New SMEs in priority sectors (Tech, Sourcing) may be eligible for specific 2-year profit tax exemptions.

heroData.title: MSA & Legal in Cambodia

steps.title: Requirement Scoping
steps.description: Defining the scope of services, KPIs, and liability caps relevant to the Cambodian business environment.

steps.title: Khmer-English Drafting
steps.description: Preparing dual-language contracts. While English is common, Khmer versions are often required for official filings or court proceedings.

steps.title: Dispute Resolution Clause
steps.description: Incorporating arbitration clauses specifying the National Commercial Arbitration Centre (NCAC) in Phnom Penh for local disputes.

steps.title: Execution & Stamping
steps.description: Assisting with proper signing protocols and ensuring documents are correctly stamped and witness-signed for validity.

items.title: Civil Code Basis
items.text: Cambodian contract law is based on the Civil Code (2007). Understanding 'offer and acceptance' and 'force majeure' definitions within this framework is critical.

items.title: Enforceability
items.text: Ensure your MSA specifies a clear governing law. While local law is often preferred for local assets, international arbitration is common for cross-border agreements.

items.title: NCAC Arbitration
items.text: The NCAC provides a faster, more specialized alternative to the traditional court system for commercial disputes in Cambodia.

items.title: Master Service Agreement
items.description: The primary framework for long-term B2B partnerships in Cambodia.

items.title: Non-Disclosure Agreement
items.description: Crucial for protecting trade secrets in a competitive labor market.

items.title: SLA & KPI Annexes
items.description: Detailed performance metrics for local vendor management.

items.title: Conflict of Interest Docs
items.description: Formalizing ethical standards for vendors and partners in the local market.

faqs.question: Are electronic signatures valid?
faqs.answer: Electronic signatures are increasingly recognized under the Law on E-Commerce, but wet-ink signatures and company stamps remain the gold standard for high-value contracts.

faqs.question: What is 'Stamp Duty'?
faqs.answer: Certain legal documents, like property transfers or government contracts, require a physical stamp duty payment to be considered fully enforceable.

faqs.question: Can I use foreign law for contracts?
faqs.answer: For cross-border deals, foreign governing law (like Singapore) is common, but Cambodian courts may still apply local mandatory laws for local performance.

items.title: Governing Law
items.text: While Singapore law is common for international contracts, always ensure local labor or property terms comply with the Cambodian Civil Code.

items.title: Translation Precedence
items.text: Specify which language version (Khmer or English) takes precedence in case of any linguistic ambiguity.

items.title: Termination Clauses
items.text: Clearly define fixed-period vs rolling terms to avoid accidental conversion to Undetermined Duration contracts.

heroData.title: Software in Cambodia
heroData.subtitle: Digital transformation for local businesses
heroData.description: Implementing enterprise-grade software solutions built for the Cambodian market. From local ERP systems like Maqsu to integrations with the national Bakong payment system.
heroData.bestFor: Enterprises looking to modernize operations and digital payments

steps.title: Gap Analysis
steps.description: Evaluating your current workflows (Sales, Inventory, Finance) and identifying bottlenecks in the Cambodian local context.

steps.title: Local System Selection
steps.description: Matching your needs with local champions like Maqsu or global leaders with local support like Microsoft Dynamics 365.

steps.title: Bakong/Payment Integration
steps.description: Enabling KHQR and digital payment workflows through the National Bank of Cambodia's Bakong blockchain system.

steps.title: Training & Localization
steps.description: Ensuring the software interface and reporting (Invoices, Tax reports) are fully localized in Khmer and English.

items.title: The Bakong Revolution
items.text: Cambodia leads the region in retail blockchain payments. Any customer-facing software should ideally integrate with Bakong for seamless KHQR payments.

items.title: Connectivity Issues
items.text: While Phnom Penh has excellent fiber, regional sites may require offline-capable systems or robust mobile synchronization.

items.title: Local ERP Advantage
items.text: Local ERP systems like Maqsu or Cuscen often have 'out-of-the-box' GDT and NSSF reporting features that global systems lack.

items.title: POS & Retail
items.description: Cloud-based Point of Sale systems with integrated inventory and KHQR payment support.

items.title: ERP & CRM
items.description: Unified business management systems tailored for Cambodian tax and commercial regulations.

items.title: Fintech & E-Wallet
items.description: Solutions for microfinance and digital wallet ecosystems supporting Bakong.

items.title: Logistics & Supply Chain
items.description: Last-mile delivery and warehouse management software for the growing e-commerce sector.

items.title: Payment Gateways
items.text: Integration with local gateways like ABA Pay or Pi Pay is essential for consumer-facing software.

items.title: Cybersecurity Law
items.text: Stay aware of the evolving Law on Cybercrime and E-commerce Law regarding consumer data protection.

items.title: IT Talent Pool
items.text: Phnom Penh is developing a strong community of tech talent, especially in React and mobile development.

faqs.question: Can I use global AWS/Azure instances?
faqs.answer: Yes, Cambodia has no strict data residency laws preventing the use of global cloud providers, though latency is best managed via regional hubs like Singapore.

faqs.question: Are there local IT support firms?
faqs.answer: Yes, there is a thriving ecosystem of IT managed service providers in Phnom Penh for hardware and software troubleshooting.

faqs.question: What is the MAQSU ERP?
faqs.answer: MAQSU is a leading local ERP provider frequently used by Cambodian SMEs for GAAP/CFRS compliant financial reporting.

heroData.title: Marketing in Cambodia
heroData.subtitle: Capture the Cambodian digital consumer
heroData.description: Unlock growth in one of Southeast Asia's fastest-growing digital economies. From Facebook and TikTok campaigns to localized KOL (Influencer) strategies and Telegram community management.
heroData.bestFor: Brands looking to establish a local pulse and drive sales

steps.title: Facebook Domination
steps.description: Facebook is the 'internet' for most Cambodians. Strategy must focus on high-engagement posts and localized Khmer content.

steps.title: TikTok & Short-Form Video
steps.description: Rapidly growing among Gen Z. Use creative storytelling and trending local audio to capture attention.

steps.title: Telegram Communities
steps.description: Crucial for B2B and direct customer support. Telegram is the primary communication tool for professional and retail users alike.

steps.title: KOL & Influencer Sourcing
steps.description: Collaborating with local influencers who command high trust. Content must feel authentic and relatable to Cambodian values.

items.title: Mobile-First Population
items.text: Over 70% of Cambodians are active on social media. All campaigns must be optimized for mobile-first consumption.

items.title: Localization is Key
items.text: Generic English content often fails. Direct translation into Khmer with cultural nuances is mandatory for mass-market appeal.

items.title: Social Commerce
items.text: Cambodians love to buy directly through Facebook Messenger and Telegram. High responsiveness to chats is equivalent to high conversion.

items.title: Digital Performance
items.description: Managed Meta and TikTok ads focused on lead generation and direct sales (Social Commerce).

items.title: Event & Activation
items.description: Offline-to-online marketing through physical events in Phnom Penh, Siem Reap, and Sihanoukville.

items.title: Content Production
items.description: Professional Khmer-language video and graphic design tailored for high social engagement.

items.title: SMS Marketing
items.text: High-read-rate direct messaging for promotional alerts to local Cambodian SIM holders.

faqs.question: What is a typical marketing budget?
faqs.answer: Boutique digital retainers start from $800 - $1,500/month, while large-scale influencer campaigns can vary significantly based on reach.

faqs.question: Is Google Search (SEO) effective?
faqs.answer: Google is important for high-intent searches, but social discovery (Facebook) remains the primary engine for brand awareness in Cambodia.

faqs.question: Who are the top agencies in Cambodia?
faqs.answer: Leading agencies include Havas Riverorchid, Mango Tango, and Giant Focus, who specialize in localized creative strategies.

items.title: Symbolism & Colors
items.text: Yellow and Orange are associated with Buddhism (the state religion) and can evoke trust when used respectfully.

items.title: Khmer Typography
items.text: Many modern Khmer fonts exist. Ensure your brand identity uses readable, aesthetically pleasing Khmer scripts.

items.title: Voice of the Customer
items.text: Direct, aspirational marketing works well, but always ensure it aligns with local 'cultural sensitivity' standards.
